message.content: 獅子（屬於貓科）和斑馬（屬於馬科）雖然分屬不同的目（Carnivora 與 Perissodactyla），但它們的最後共同祖先是**所有有胎盤哺乳類動物的祖先**。這個祖先大約生活在七到八億年前，屬於早期的有胎盤哺乳類（Placentalia）祖先。

The answer: Both lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus zebra) are mammals, more specifically they belong to different families: lions are Felidae (cat family), zebras are Equidae (horse family). Their common ancestor would be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora (for lions) and the order Perissodactyla (for zebras). Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia, family Felidae. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla, family Equidae. The last common ancestor of all mammals? But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the Felidae and Equidae families, which would be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla diverged from the same ancestor as other orders like Artiodactyla, Primates, etc. The last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals, which is the last common ancestor of all mammals. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the Felidae and Equidae families, which would be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals. That ancestor would have lived around 70-80 million years ago. So answer: "the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 70-80 million years ago." Or "the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals."
